subject: use of factor to discriminate on two factors.

messages.author: 88efb44254d64d30
messages.subject: use of factor to discriminate on two factors.
parts:
I have a large dataset which contains a CD.Mean column as well as two
columns which I would like to use as factors in my plots; Overlap and
Shape. Shape may be "rectangular", "circular", or other types.
Overlap is simply a number such as 100, 200, etc.

The following will use the Overlap of all of the shape types.

qplot(CD.Mean,data=alldata, geom="density",fill = factor(Overlap),
alpha=I(0.5)) +
opts(title = title ) +
labs(list(x = "CD Mean", y = "Density")) +
opts(plot.title = theme_text(size=14, lineheight=.8, face="bold")) +
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(face="bold", colour="black",
size=12)) +
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(face="bold", colour="black",
size=12))

This works very well and labels each of the Overlap values in the
legend very nicely.

I would like to separate out as a factor the Overlap for a given Type.

Ideally, and I know this is improper syntax, I would like to do this..

factor( Type, Overlap)

which would separately plot all of the unique combinations of type and
overlap and label them accordingly in the legend.

or

factor(Type=="rectangular", Overlap)

which would filter on the fly the rectangular from the circular
overlap factors.

Sorry for my new learner question!
Bob
